differences.title: 1. METADATA MANAGEMENT
differences.leftDesc: Delta Lake uses a transaction log (JSON files) to record every commit, ensuring atomic operations and data versioning for reliable ACID properties.
differences.rightDesc: Iceberg manages metadata in JSON files representing table state, enabling snapshot isolation and atomic commits without explicit transaction logs per operation.

differences.title: 2. CONCURRENCY CONTROL
differences.leftDesc: Delta Lake employs optimistic concurrency control, detecting conflicts by checking the transaction log before committing new writes to prevent lost updates.
differences.rightDesc: Iceberg also uses optimistic concurrency, checking metadata files to ensure no concurrent modifications have occurred before finalizing a write operation.

differences.title: 3. TIME TRAVEL
differences.leftDesc: Delta Lake allows querying previous table versions by referencing version numbers or timestamps stored in its transaction log for historical analysis.
differences.rightDesc: Iceberg enables time travel by querying specific snapshots identified by their metadata file paths or commit timestamps.

differences.title: 4. PARTITION EVOLUTION
differences.leftDesc: Delta Lake typically requires manual re-partitioning or explicit schema updates to change partitioning schemes, though evolving it is possible with careful management.
differences.rightDesc: Iceberg supports hidden partitioning, automatically deriving partition values from data columns without requiring users to manage separate partition columns.

differences.title: 5. SCHEMA EVOLUTION
differences.leftDesc: Delta Lake enforces schema enforcement by default, preventing writes that don't match the table's schema, but allows schema evolution with specific commands.
differences.rightDesc: Iceberg supports schema evolution natively, allowing column additions, deletions, and renames without rewriting existing data, maintaining compatibility.

differences.title: 6. TABLE OPERATIONS
differences.leftDesc: Delta Lake guarantees ACID transactions through its transaction log, ensuring data integrity and reliable concurrent reads and writes.
differences.rightDesc: Iceberg uses atomic commits by atomically updating metadata pointers, providing isolation and consistency for table operations.

differences.title: 7. CATALOG INTEGRATION
differences.leftDesc: Delta Lake integrates tightly with Hive Metastore and Unity Catalog, providing a unified metadata layer for tables across different engines.
differences.rightDesc: Iceberg offers flexible catalog support, working with Hive Metastore, AWS Glue, and custom catalog implementations for broad compatibility.
